limits.what: fcc lattices, up to 8 atoms, an estimated 90 s of compiled wasm; larger runs natively with dft/run.sh

engines.name: dft-bands
engines.title: Band structure of a crystal, from a POSCAR, a CIF or a pw.x input
engines.source:
#! engine dft-bands
#! title Band structure of a crystal, from a POSCAR, a CIF or a pw.x input
#! program dft/pwdft_it
#! input crystal: poscar | cif | qe-pw | xyz+cell
#! input settings: ecut, kmesh, smearing, bands (defaults from dft/ref/materials.py)
#! output bands, total-energy
#! limit tab: fcc lattices, up to 8 atoms, an estimated 90 s of compiled wasm; larger runs natively with dft/run.sh
#! validated si: dft/si_it_check.viv
#! validated gaas: dft/gaas_it_check.viv
#
# The DFT engine as a program you feed a crystal. An adapter (www/src/lib/engines/)
# turns a POSCAR, a CIF, a Quantum ESPRESSO pw.x input or an extended XYZ file
# into an input deck of the kind dft/ref/make_deck.py writes, and this program
# runs it through the iterative engine, dft/pwdft_it.viv.
#
# The deck arrives in one of two ways:
#
#   interpreted  the adapter's deck text replaces the input block below
#   compiled     this program is compiled once, with silicon's deck in that place,
#                and engines/build-wasm.mjs adds a loader at the DECK_LOADED line:
#                it reads the reader's deck from standard input and overwrites
#                every deck variable by name, so one module runs any deck. With
#                nothing on standard input it computes silicon.

# ---- input: the page replaces everything from here to "end of input"
from dft.si import EIG_TOL, MAXIT, NBANDS, NSEG, SMEAR
# the reference: set by the page when the crystal and settings are exactly a deck dft/ has
#: HAS_REF   1 when the values below are dft/'s numpy reference for this very deck
#: REF_ETOT  its total energy, hartree (from dft/<material>_it_check.viv)
#: REFPATH   its lowest REF_NB bands at every path point, eV
HAS_REF = 0.0
REF_ETOT = 0.0
REF_NB = 0.0
REFPATH = zeros(1, 1)
# ---- end of input
#: DECK_LOADED  marks where the deck ends: the compiled engine loads the reader's deck here
DECK_LOADED = 1.0
import dft.kmesh
from dft.pw_common import NELEC, NPTS, PATHX
from dft.pwdft_it import BANDRES, DRHO, EIGRES, EREF, ETOT, EVB, ITER, NVAL
from engines.precise import precise_hi, precise_lo, precise_mid

# ---- the report: what the page reads ----------------------------------------
#
# ETOT is the engine's total energy, which leaves out the ion-ion (Ewald) term
# (dft/README.md): it is comparable between runs on the same atoms, not between
# structures.
show ETOT
ETOT_HI = precise_hi(ETOT)
ETOT_MID = precise_mid(ETOT)
ETOT_LO = precise_lo(ETOT)
show ETOT_HI
show ETOT_MID
show ETOT_LO
show EREF
show NELEC
show NBANDS
show BANDRES

#: GAP  for an insulator, the lowest empty band along the path, from the
#:      valence-band top: the gap along L - Gamma - X (0 for a metal)
GAP = 0.0
if SMEAR <= 0.0 and NVAL < NBANDS {
    GAP = 1.0e9
    for p to NPTS {
        if EVB[p, NVAL] < GAP { GAP = EVB[p, NVAL] }
    }
}
show GAP

#: REF_DE     |ETOT - REF_ETOT|, when there is a reference
#: REF_DBAND  the largest |band - reference band| anywhere on the path, eV
if HAS_REF > 0.5 {
    REF_DE = abs(ETOT - REF_ETOT)
    REF_DBAND = 0.0
    for p to NPTS {
        for b to REF_NB {
            d = abs(EVB[p, b] - REFPATH[p, b])
            if d > REF_DBAND { REF_DBAND = d }
        }
    }
    show REF_DE
    show REF_DBAND
}

test "SCF converged: density, energy, and every occupied band's residual" {
    assert_lt(DRHO, 1.0e-8)
    assert_lt(EIGRES, EIG_TOL)
    assert_lt(ITER, MAXIT)
}
test "every band-path point converged" {
    assert_lt(BANDRES, EIG_TOL)
}

figure("LDA band structure", "wavevector along the path", "energy (eV)")
for b to NBANDS {
    e = zeros(NPTS)
    for p to NPTS {
        e[p] = EVB[p, b]
    }
    plot(PATHX, e, "band")
}
#| The path's corners, where PATHX puts them: corner c is point c * NSEG.
xtick("L", PATHX[0])
xtick("Γ", PATHX[NSEG])
xtick("X", PATHX[NPTS - 1])
#| Energies are measured from zero: the Fermi level for a metal, the
#| valence-band top for an insulator.
XEND = PATHX[NPTS - 1]
hline("zero", 0.0)
if SMEAR > 0.0 {
    label("zero-label", "Fermi level", 0.86 * XEND, 0.0)
}
else {
    label("zero-label", "valence band top", 0.84 * XEND, 0.0)
}
#| An insulator's gap: from the valence-band top to the lowest empty band.
if GAP > 0.0 {
    fill_between("gap", PATHX, zeros(NPTS), zeros(NPTS) + GAP)
    label("gap-label", "gap", 0.25 * XEND, 0.5 * GAP)
}

inputs.how: basis (sto-3g | 6-31g | 6-31g* | cc-pvdz | def2-svp), charge, spin, method (rhf | uhf | rohf), spherical or cartesian

engines.name: hf-energy
engines.title: Hartree-Fock energy of a molecule, from an XYZ file and a basis name
engines.source:
#! engine hf-energy
#! title Hartree-Fock energy of a molecule, from an XYZ file and a basis name
#! program lib/hf/scf
#! input molecule: xyz
#! input settings: basis (sto-3g | 6-31g | 6-31g* | cc-pvdz | def2-svp), charge, spin, method (rhf | uhf | rohf), spherical or cartesian
#! output total-energy, orbital-energies
#! limit tab: elements H to Ar, up to an estimated 60 s in the interpreter; larger runs natively with viv run
#! validated water 6-31g: lib/hfref/water_631g.viv
#! validated water cc-pvdz: lib/hfref/water_ccpvdz.viv
#
# lib/hf as a program you feed a molecule. An adapter (www/src/lib/engines/
# molecule.js) reads an XYZ file, looks the basis up in a table taken from
# PySCF (www/src/lib/engines/hf-bases.json), and writes the three basis packs
# lib/hf takes: atoms (Z, x, y, z in bohr), shells and
# primitives. This program wraps them in a `Molecule` (lib/hf/molecule) and
# runs lib/hf/scf's `scf_with` on it, with every stage at its production
# member; the `ScfResult` carries the energy and the orbital energies.

from hf.scf import scf_with
from hf.molecule import mol_enuc, mol_nalpha, mol_nbeta, Molecule, molecule_packs
from hf.opts import scf_defaults, SCF_RHF, SCF_ROHF, SCF_UHF, ScfOptions
import basis.pople631g
from hf.mole import molecule
from engines.precise import precise_hi, precise_lo, precise_mid
from hfref.water_631g import WATER631G_E_RHF

# ---- input: the page replaces everything from here to "end of input".
# This default is water in 6-31G at the geometry of tools/hf_reference.py,
# written as PySCF takes it (lib/hf/mole); the page writes the three packs
# from its XYZ adapter instead.
MOL_DEFAULT = molecule("O 0 0 0; H 0 -0.757 0.587; H 0 0.757 0.587", "6-31g")
#: MOL_ATOMS      [natm, 4]: Z, x, y, z in bohr
#: MOL_SHELLS     [nsh, 8]: atom, l, nprim, p0, cart0, sph0, ncart, nsph
#: MOL_PRIMS      [nprim, 2]: exponent, raw contraction coefficient
#: MOL_CHARGE     net charge
#: MOL_SPIN       Na - Nb, as PySCF's spin
#: MOL_SPHERICAL  1 for spherical AOs (PySCF's default), 0 for Cartesian
#: MOL_METHOD     0 auto (RHF when closed, else UHF), 1 RHF, 2 UHF, 3 ROHF
MOL_ATOMS = MOL_DEFAULT.atoms
MOL_SHELLS = MOL_DEFAULT.shells
MOL_PRIMS = MOL_DEFAULT.prims
MOL_CHARGE = 0.0
MOL_SPIN = 0.0
MOL_SPHERICAL = 1.0
MOL_METHOD = 0.0
#: HAS_REF  1 when REF_E is the lib/hfref energy for exactly this molecule, basis and state
#: REF_E    that energy, hartree (PySCF, conv_tol 1e-12)
HAS_REF = 1.0
REF_E = WATER631G_E_RHF
# ---- end of input

narrate "integrals and SCF"
MOL = Molecule { charge: MOL_CHARGE, spin: MOL_SPIN, cart: 1.0 - MOL_SPHERICAL, ..molecule_packs(MOL_ATOMS, MOL_SHELLS, MOL_PRIMS) }
RESULT = scf_with(MOL, ScfOptions { method: MOL_METHOD, ..scf_defaults() })

NAO = len(RESULT.density)
METHOD = RESULT.method
E_TOTAL = RESULT.energy
E_NUC = mol_enuc(MOL)
NALPHA = mol_nalpha(MOL)
NBETA = mol_nbeta(MOL)
CONVERGED = RESULT.converged
GRADIENT = RESULT.grad
ITERATIONS = RESULT.iterations
E_HI = precise_hi(E_TOTAL)
E_MID = precise_mid(E_TOTAL)
E_LO = precise_lo(E_TOTAL)
show NAO
show METHOD
show NALPHA
show NBETA
show E_TOTAL
show E_HI
show E_MID
show E_LO
show E_NUC
show CONVERGED
show GRADIENT
show ITERATIONS
if METHOD != SCF_RHF {
    S2 = RESULT.s2
    show S2
}

# ---- orbital energies: the eigenvalues of the last Fock matrix, which the
# result carries per spin. The SCF stops when F D S - S D F is below 1e-9, so
# these are the eigenvalues of the converged Fock matrix to that accuracy.
# ROHF has no unique orbital energies (they depend on how the effective Fock
# matrix is built), so none are shown for it.
narrate "orbital energies"
if METHOD != SCF_ROHF {
    NMO = len(RESULT.alpha.mo_energy)
    MO_ALPHA = RESULT.alpha.mo_energy
    show NMO
    show MO_ALPHA
    if METHOD == SCF_UHF {
        MO_BETA = RESULT.beta.mo_energy
        show MO_BETA
    }
}

test "the SCF converged: energy change below 1e-12 and max |FDS - SDF| below 1e-9" {
    assert_near(CONVERGED, 1.0, 0.0)
}

#: REF_DE  |E - REF_E|, when there is a reference
if HAS_REF > 0.5 {
    REF_DE = abs(E_TOTAL - REF_E)
    show REF_DE
}

# GTH/HGH pseudopotentials, LDA (Pade). GENERATED by dft/pseudo/make_pseudo.py
# from CP2K's GTH_POTENTIALS table -- do not edit by hand.
#   S. Goedecker, M. Teter, J. Hutter, PRB 54, 1703 (1996)
#   C. Hartwigsen, S. Goedecker, J. Hutter, PRB 58, 3641 (1998)
#   species 0: Si GTH-PADE-q4
NSPEC = 1.0
GTH_NLOC = 4.0         #: GTH_NLOC  coefficients C1..C4 of the local part
GTH_NL = 4.0           #: GTH_NL  angular momentum channels, l = 0 .. 3
GTH_NPMAX = 3.0        #: GTH_NPMAX  at most this many projectors in one channel
ZION = zeros(NSPEC)
RLOC = zeros(NSPEC)
CLOC = zeros(NSPEC, GTH_NLOC)
NPRJ = zeros(NSPEC, GTH_NL)       #: NPRJ  projectors per (species, l)
RPRJ = zeros(NSPEC, GTH_NL)       #: RPRJ  projector radius r_l per (species, l)
HPRJ = zeros(NSPEC, GTH_NL, GTH_NPMAX, GTH_NPMAX) #: HPRJ  the coupling matrix h^l_ij per (species, l)
ZION[0] = 4.0
RLOC[0] = 0.44
CLOC[0, 0] = -7.33610297
NPRJ[0, 0] = 2.0
RPRJ[0, 0] = 0.42273813

HPRJ[0, 0, 1, 0] = -1.26189397

NPRJ[0, 1] = 1.0
RPRJ[0, 1] = 0.48427842
HPRJ[0, 1, 0, 0] = 2.72701346

# --- the crystal: an fcc lattice ---------------------------------------------
ALAT = 10.26                          #: ALAT  lattice constant, bohr
A = [[0.0, ALAT / 2.0, ALAT / 2.0],
     [ALAT / 2.0, 0.0, ALAT / 2.0],
     [ALAT / 2.0, ALAT / 2.0, 0.0]]   #: A  primitive vectors, one per ROW

ATSPEC = [0.0, 0.0]        #: ATSPEC  species index of each atom

          [-0.125, -0.125, -0.125]]   #: ATFRAC  positions, fractions of A

# --- the calculation --------------------------------------------------------
ECUT = 10.0                           #: ECUT  plane-wave cutoff, hartree
NBANDS = 8.0                         #: NBANDS  bands computed at every k-point
SMEAR = 0.0                          #: SMEAR  Fermi-Dirac width, hartree; 0 for an insulator
NKMESH = 2.0                         #: NKMESH  the k-mesh is NKMESH^3, shifted (dft/kmesh.viv)

SCF_TOL = 1.0e-9
MAXIT = 80.0
NITER = 3.0                           #: NITER  LOBPCG steps per k-point per SCF iteration (iterative engine)
NITER_BANDS = 60.0                    #: NITER_BANDS  at most this many LOBPCG steps per band-path point, from a cold start
EIG_TOL = 1.0e-5                      #: EIG_TOL  residual norm |H psi - eps psi| every band that matters must reach

# --- the band path: L -> Gamma -> X ------------------------------------------
NCORNER = 3.0
CORNER = [[0.5, 0.5, 0.5],
          [0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
          [0.5, 0.0, 0.5]]
